supersedes.defense.waves_per_reward: R15: the R12 SCRIPT_PARAM_GLOBAL_AT_ENTRY owner wrote the level parameter into the WaveDefense instance environment at the trigger entry. Live 2026-10-01 (DLL e5d9b61b, addon 4c70b5ec): the write ran (EE 581.400 'minWavesToComplete 3 -> 1') but the checkpoint after waves 1 and 2 did not open. The environment is not owned by the entry write: the engine's script-parameter applier writes the trigger's level values into the instance environment natively (44.0.2 RVA 0x181CAE0 via ApplyScriptParams 0x175C710 / 0x1280F60 / 0x0C6DD40) and the script-run loop at 0x0A77E90 re-applies them to an already existing instance before running it, without the busy check of the entity path 0x02EB8F0 (which call re-applied them in the live session is not identified offline). The four readers are the owner of the decision input; R15 pins them.

rows.variant: every WaveDefense trigger (regular, Infested, Orokin, 1999 Hollvania, Kahl); Duviri and Descendia circle arenas skip the rotation code (the value still feeds their fixed-length session-hide rule)

P48 i960 GETIMPORT minWavesToComplete -> LOADN: fixed length, hide the session in the last rotation when count - N <= waves done (L8934)

limits.basis: operand domain guard only (0 would make the checkpoint test x % 0, which never matches); LOADN domain 1..32767; gameplay-safe range not established offline

rows.evidence: WaveDefend 44.0.2 (body 1a1354d153712f9d) reads the trigger parameter _minWavesToComplete only as the single-name import GETIMPORT #69d6d911 at P48 i960/i1122 and P36 i238/i307 (U44 opcode 0x35, aux count 1, id0 -> hashed name 69d6d911); no other instruction of the 5,473 installed bodies names the hash. The import constant is never resolved at load (luau_load resolves imports only when the loader thread's globals are safeenv; lua_setsafeenv has two callers, both fresh instance environments, and lua_setreadonly is called only by table.freeze, so no sandbox marks the globals safe), so every read is the live instance-environment lookup at decision time. R15 rewrites each import (instruction word and aux word) into LOADN A, N twice: the same register, the same instruction count and jump targets, no environment read. With the row off the module is stock.
